newsitem.title: USA: Allegiance says lower Q1 SG&A offset sales dip.
newsitem.headline: Allegiance says lower Q1 SG&A offset sales dip.

text.p: Allegiance Corp said that in the first quarter it cut selling, general and administrative expenses by $7 million to help offset sales declines during the quarter.
The company has said it expects sales this year to be roughly flat in 1997 compared with 1996.
The healthcare products concern said it improved its gross profit margin by 60 basis points on the quarter.
Allegiance on Wednesday reported it earned $21.0 million for the quarter ended March 31, compared with pro forma net income of $15.1 million a year ago.

Sales were reduced by five percent on the quarter to $1.06 billion as the company continued efforts to reduce sales of less-profitable products and services. In the 1996 first quarter, pro forma sales were $1.11 billion.

The company said it is also putting greater emphasis on generating free cash flow, or cash flow from operations less capital expenditures and dividend payments. The company produced $62.5 million of free cash flow in the first quarter.

Allegiance was formed in September 1996, when it spun off from Baxter International Inc. "We continue to expect a solid operating performance for 1997," said Lester B. Knight, chairman and chief executive officer.
